questions.q: What table stores the parent REST Message record?
options: sys_rest_message_fn
sys_rest_message
sys_ws_operation
sys_web_service
questions.explain: sys_rest_message is the parent record holding the base Endpoint and default Authentication Profile; sys_rest_message_fn is its child Function table.

questions.q: A REST Message named WeatherAPI has its Endpoint set to https://api.weatherservice.com/v1 and its Authentication Profile set to WeatherAPI Basic Auth. What does every Function under this REST Message inherit by default?
options: Nothing — each Function must set its own Endpoint and Authentication Profile
Only the HTTP method
The base Endpoint and the Authentication Profile, unless a Function overrides them
Only the request headers
questions.explain: The parent record's Endpoint and Authentication Profile are the defaults every child Function inherits, which is why rotating a credential once fixes every operation underneath it.

questions.q:
Given this configuration:

Function: getForecast
  HTTP Method: GET
  Endpoint: /forecast?city=${city}&days=${days}

What do ${city} and ${days} represent?
options: Comments that ServiceNow ignores at request time
Placeholders substituted by script before the request is sent
Required SOAP namespace declarations
Literal query string values that never change
questions.explain: ${name} is real placeholder syntax inside a Function's Endpoint or Content field, filled in at runtime — Lesson 6 covers the script call that does the substitution.

questions.q: Why does ServiceNow split a REST Message into one parent record plus separate child Function records, instead of storing method, path, and base URL all on one record?
options: It doesn't — REST Messages have no child records
Because the base connection (URL, credential) is shared across operations, while each operation needs its own method, path, headers, and body
Because ServiceNow requires every table to have at least one child table
Purely for historical reasons with no functional benefit
questions.explain: The base Endpoint and Authentication Profile describe the external system as a whole and rarely change; each Function describes one distinct operation against that system.

questions.q: A REST Message is outbound. What is the inbound equivalent you'll study in Chapter 4, and what's the key difference in direction?
options: A Scripted REST API — ServiceNow exposes it so an external system can call ServiceNow, the opposite direction of a REST Message
Another REST Message — there is no inbound equivalent
A MID Server — it has nothing to do with direction
An Authentication Profile — it only governs credentials, not direction
questions.explain: A REST Message is ServiceNow calling out; a Scripted REST API is something else calling in. Same HTTP concepts, opposite direction, different records.
